title: Fourier coefficient from near-perfect acceptance
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb F_2^n$, and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$. Suppose $0\le\varepsilon<1$, every nonzero frequency has vector Fourier coefficient under $\phi$ of absolute value at most $\varepsilon$, and the derandomized BLR acceptance probability of $f$ under $\phi$ is $1-\delta$, where $(1+\varepsilon)/2\le(1-2\delta)^2$. Then some $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$ satisfies $\sqrt{1-2\delta-\varepsilon}/\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\le |\widehat{\operatorname{sgn}(f)}(\gamma)|$, where the coefficient is the vector Fourier coefficient of the real sign encoding of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $\phi$ is a probability density on $\mathbb F_2^n$
All nonzero vector Fourier coefficients of $\phi$ have absolute value at most $\varepsilon$
The derandomized BLR acceptance probability equals $1-\delta$
